summary: This paper presents an efficient fault-tolerant ancilla preparation method for quantum BCH codes by leveraging their cyclic symmetry to optimize entanglement-distillation protocols. The approach reduces required ancilla qubits by more than half compared to standard distillation while achieving lower logical error rates, with threshold analysis demonstrating code rates 2–4× higher than the Steane code at comparable distances.
motivation: Quantum BCH codes offer high encoding rates and large code distances at moderate block sizes, but lacked practical fault-tolerant state preparation schemes and realistic performance benchmarks needed for implementation on highly-connected platforms like neutral atom systems.
method: A two-stage approach combining non-fault-tolerant preparation with entanglement distillation, where cyclic shifts $R$ and Frobenius shifts $F$ from the automorphism group $C_n \rtimes F_m$ permute error patterns among ancilla blocks to eliminate malignant fault patterns and reduce ancilla overhead from $(t+1)$-to-$1$ to $t$-to-$1$ or better protocols.
result: For codes $\llbracket 31,11,5 \rrbracket$, $\llbracket 63,27,7 \rrbracket$, and $\llbracket 127,71,9 \rrbracket$, ancilla requirements reduced to $4/9$, $4/16$, and $6/25$ of standard levels; circuit-level simulations confirm strict fault tolerance; scaling thresholds for codes up to $n=255$ show $\llbracket 255,159,13 \rrbracket$ maintains Steane-comparable threshold $\approx 10^{-3}$ while achieving rate $0.624$ versus $0.086$ for surface codes.
